title: nhbot tech tree
about: Everything that we must build to take a dwarvish Valkyrie through the Gnomish Mines and Sokoban. A node can start when all of its needs are built. Set a node to done in the same commit as its work.

phases.name: Record
phases.summary: The bot records what the AI needs: events, incidents and batch results.

phases.name: Read the screen
phases.summary: Each frame becomes facts: messages, status, map, inventory, prompts.

phases.name: Act and remember
phases.summary: Send keys safely, choose between skills, remember each level.

phases.name: Move
phases.summary: Walk anywhere, explore, find the way down.

phases.name: Survive
phases.summary: Fight, eat and pray well enough to reach depth 5.

phases.name: Grow stronger
phases.summary: Items, Elbereth and wands. A plan for which branch comes next.

phases.name: Gnomish Mines
phases.summary: Walk among peaceful gnomes and dwarves down to Minetown.

phases.name: Sokoban
phases.summary: Find Sokoban and push boulders to solve the first level.

phases.name: Finish both branches
phases.summary: Clear the Sokoban zoo, take the prize, reach Mines' End.

nodes.name: Project and CI
nodes.done_when: CI runs ruff, the format check, mypy and pytest on each push.

nodes.name: NLE adapter
nodes.done_when: A seed gives the same game each time, and the bot sees all prompts.
nodes.why: Only one class talks to NLE, so tests can use recorded frames.

nodes.name: Game loop
nodes.done_when: GameLoop plays a game and tells each listener about each step.

nodes.name: Watch mode
nodes.done_when: You can watch, pause and step a seeded game in the terminal.

nodes.name: Run summary
nodes.done_when: Each game prints one line: steps, turn and max depth.

nodes.name: Event log
nodes.done_when: Each game writes events.jsonl. Each line has the game id, turn, depth, position and the event fields.
nodes.why: The AI reads what happened in the whole game, not a short log for humans.

nodes.name: Flight recorder
nodes.done_when: A death, an exception or a loop saves one bundle of less than 200 KB: the last 50 screens, the last 500 events and the state.
nodes.why: Each failure becomes data that the AI can study.

nodes.name: Screen samples
nodes.done_when: The first time that a new prompt or screen type appears, one copy goes to samples/.
nodes.why: Observe first, then write code (shadow mode).

nodes.name: Batch runner
nodes.done_when: nhbot.batch --seeds 1-20 plays the games in parallel and prints the median depth and the top causes of death.
nodes.why: A change must improve a metric on the same seeds.

nodes.name: Replay and incident to test
nodes.done_when: A bundle from a death replays to the same decision, and a tool makes a test from it.

nodes.name: Checked assumptions
nodes.done_when: At the end of each game, a report lists each assumption as not checked, confirmed or failed.

nodes.name: Messages
nodes.done_when: Golden screens give the expected messages, also when several messages share the top line.

nodes.name: Status
nodes.done_when: Hunger, conditions (blind, confused, stunned and others) and encumbrance come as named values.

nodes.name: Map from glyphs
nodes.done_when: Golden screens give walls, floor, doors, stairs, fountains, altars, traps, boulders, items, monsters and the pet.
nodes.why: A glyph number tells the exact monster. A letter does not: a d can be a jackal or a hell hound.

nodes.name: Inventory
nodes.done_when: Each item has its letter, count, name, blessed or cursed if known, and worn or wielded.

nodes.name: Prompts and menus
nodes.done_when: Each sampled prompt maps to a known question, and menus of several pages are read in full.

nodes.name: Monster and object data
nodes.done_when: tools/gen_data.py makes data/monsters.json (with attacks from monst.c) and data/objects.json.
nodes.why: The fight and food rules read monster facts from data, not from hand-written code.

prior.text: NLE gives level, speed, AC, MR, resistances and flags for 381 monsters, but no attacks.

nodes.name: Action executor
nodes.done_when: No game stops on an unknown prompt in 20 seeded games. Each action checks its result on the next frame (verify after act).

nodes.name: Skills and arbiter
nodes.done_when: Each system (Elbereth, eating, shops and others) is a Skill class with a priority. The arbiter runs the highest one. A flag turns each skill off.
nodes.why: A new system is one new file, and each skill can be measured alone.

nodes.name: Level memory
nodes.done_when: The bot keeps each tile, door, stair, trap and item that it saw on each level, also after it leaves the level.

nodes.name: Dungeon graph
nodes.done_when: The bot knows where each staircase goes and which levels are in the Mines or in Sokoban.

nodes.name: Threat model
nodes.done_when: Each monster in view gets a danger score from its data and from the hero's level and HP.

nodes.name: Pathfinding
nodes.done_when: The bot walks to a chosen tile around walls and known traps, and never moves diagonally into or out of a doorway.

nodes.name: Doors
nodes.done_when: The bot opens closed doors and kicks locked doors, but never a shop door.

nodes.name: Exploration
nodes.done_when: On 5 seeds, the bot sees all of level 1 and finds the down stairs.

nodes.name: Hidden passages
nodes.done_when: When no exit is known, the bot searches dead ends and walls and finds the way on (coverage search).

nodes.name: Stairs
nodes.done_when: The bot goes down or up stairs when its goal tells it to, and records where each staircase goes.

nodes.name: Melee
nodes.done_when: The bot attacks adjacent hostile monsters, and never a peaceful monster or its pet.

nodes.name: Retreat
nodes.done_when: The bot leaves a fight that it cannot win, toward the up stairs or a corridor.

nodes.name: Hunger and eating
nodes.done_when: No deaths by starvation in 20 games, and the bot eats only safe food.
nodes.why: Seen in play: a random walk that never ate fainted from hunger at turn 1036 and died (seed 7).

prior.text: A corpse older than about 50 turns can be tainted, which can kill. Lichen and lizard corpses do not rot.

nodes.name: Prayer
nodes.done_when: The bot prays only in real trouble and only when the timeout is low. It records the turn of each prayer.

prior.text: The prayer timeout starts near 300. In major trouble (HP 5 or less, or at most 1/7 of max HP), a prayer is safe when the timeout is below 200 and Luck is not negative.

nodes.name: Safety rules
nodes.done_when: Each rule of brief section 10 has a source and a test: floating eye, cockatrice, bad corpses, peaceful monsters and shopkeepers.

prior.text: Do not melee a floating eye unless blind or with free action. Its passive attack can paralyse the hero for a long time.

nodes.name: M1: depth 5
nodes.done_when: The bot reaches depth 5 in most of 20 seeded games.

nodes.name: Elbereth
nodes.done_when: In danger, the bot engraves Elbereth in the dust, checks that it is there, and does not attack from that square.

prior.text: In 3.6, most monsters respect it. Humans (@), minotaurs, shopkeepers, guards and priests do not. An attack from the square erases it.

nodes.name: Pick up
nodes.done_when: The bot picks up food, armour, wands, rings and amulets, and stays below Burdened.

nodes.name: Wear armour
nodes.done_when: The bot wears better armour, one piece at a time, and checks its AC after each piece.

nodes.name: Item knowledge
nodes.done_when: The bot records what it learns about each appearance in this game: prices, engrave tests and effects.
nodes.why: Appearances are random in each game. A blue potion is not the same potion in the next game.

nodes.name: Healing
nodes.done_when: The bot uses known healing potions and a unicorn horn when its HP or its status needs them.

nodes.name: Wand engrave-test
nodes.done_when: The bot engrave-tests each unknown wand and records the result.

prior.text: Fire and lightning wands burn the engraving. A digging wand engraves into the floor. The message names the type of wand.

nodes.name: Wands in a fight
nodes.done_when: The bot zaps known attack wands at dangerous monsters, and digs down to escape.

nodes.name: Excalibur
nodes.done_when: At experience level 5 or more, the bot dips its long sword in a fountain until it gets Excalibur, and handles what comes out.

prior.text: Lawful, experience level 5 or more and a long sword: each #dip has a 1 in 6 chance. Other dips can bring water moccasins or a water nymph, or curse items.

nodes.name: Goals and stages
nodes.done_when: A goal stack picks the next branch (the Mines or Sokoban), and the side panel shows the current goal.

nodes.name: Pacing rule
nodes.done_when: The bot goes deeper only when its experience level meets the rule for that depth. Batch metrics set the numbers.

nodes.name: Find the Mines
nodes.done_when: On Dlvl 2 to 4, the bot finds the second down staircase and knows that it goes to the Mines.

prior.text: The Mines entrance is on Dlvl 2, 3 or 4.

nodes.name: Cave levels
nodes.done_when: The bot explores Mines levels (no rooms, no doors, irregular walls, dark parts) and finds the down stairs.

nodes.name: Peaceful crowds
nodes.done_when: The bot walks around peaceful gnomes and dwarves, waits when they block a corridor, and always answers no to "Really attack?".

prior.text: For a dwarf hero, gnomes and dwarves are peaceful. Hill orcs are still hostile.

nodes.name: Minetown map
nodes.done_when: The bot knows which Minetown layout it is on, and where the temple, the shops and the altar are.

prior.text: Minetown is on Dlvl 5 to 8 and has 7 layouts. Orcish Town (new in 3.6) has many orcs and no priest or shopkeepers.

nodes.name: M2: Minetown
nodes.done_when: The bot reaches Minetown in most of 20 seeded games.

nodes.name: Temple and altar
nodes.done_when: The bot drops items on the altar to learn which are blessed or cursed, and never angers the priest.

prior.text: An amber flash means blessed. A black flash means cursed.

nodes.name: Shops
nodes.done_when: The bot enters shops, pays for what it takes, never steals, and records prices to identify items.

prior.text: A shopkeeper blocks the door to a hero who carries a pick-axe.

nodes.name: Find Sokoban
nodes.done_when: On the level below the Oracle, the bot finds the extra up staircase and goes up into Sokoban.

prior.text: The Oracle is on Dlvl 5 to 9. The Sokoban branch is on the next level down.

nodes.name: Sokoban maps
nodes.done_when: The bot knows which of the 8 maps (4 levels, 2 layouts each) it is on.

nodes.name: Stored solutions
nodes.done_when: Each of the 8 maps has a tested list of moves in data/special_levels/.
nodes.why: Stored solutions are smaller and safer than a solver.

nodes.name: Boulder pushes
nodes.done_when: The bot checks each push. If a boulder is not where the solution expects it, the bot stops the level and saves a bundle.

prior.text: In Sokoban, boulders do not move diagonally. Breaking a boulder and some other moves cost Luck.

nodes.name: Monsters in Sokoban
nodes.done_when: When a monster blocks a push or a path, the bot fights or waits, then continues the solution from where it is.

nodes.name: M3: Sokoban level 1
nodes.done_when: The bot solves the first Sokoban level in most games that reach it.

nodes.name: The Sokoban zoo
nodes.done_when: The bot clears the zoo on the top Sokoban level and lives.

nodes.name: Sokoban complete
nodes.done_when: The bot takes the prize at the top of Sokoban.

prior.text: The prize is a bag of holding or an amulet of reflection.

nodes.name: Mines' End
nodes.done_when: The bot reaches the bottom level of the Mines and lives.

prior.text: Mines' End is on Dlvl 10 to 13.
